title: Commercial building, mechanical (fuel gas), electrical and plumbing permits for a glass studio's furnace, glory hole, kilns and exhaust, through the certificate of occupancy
question: What building and trade permits does a glass studio in Albemarle County need to install a gas-fired furnace, glory hole, kilns, torches, exhaust hoods and gas piping, how do I apply in the County's online system, what does it cost, and how are inspections and the certificate of occupancy handled?
office: Community Development Department, Building Inspections (the Building Official), with Application Services for intake; zoning, engineering, the Albemarle County Service Authority and Fire Rescue plan review as reviewers
summary: Albemarle enforces the Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code through its Community Development Department. A glass studio in an existing commercial or industrial space is a Commercial Alteration (tenant up-fit) permit, with a Change in Building Occupancy Classification where the space was something else; a new building needs a New Commercial permit against an approved site plan and VDOT approval. Every application goes in the Civic Access portal with building plans, a life-safety plan (exits, occupant loads, fire ratings, accessibility) and, where steel or other engineered systems are used, a Special Inspections Report. The gas-fired furnace, glory hole, kilns, exhaust hoods, make-up air and gas piping are mechanical work; each trade (mechanical, electrical, plumbing, gas, fire alarm, sprinkler) files its own sub-permit through a Virginia-licensed contractor. Fees are invoiced before issuance (new commercial building $0.24 per square foot up to 5,000 square feet then $0.17, minimum $90; alterations $0.20 per square foot, minimum $90; mechanical new commercial $0.04 per square foot, minimum $90; gas lines $40; plus plan review rows and a 4% surcharge). Inspections are requested in Civic Access; the certificate of occupancy follows the final building, trade, fire and zoning inspections, and a temporary certificate costs $150 per 30 days. The Health Department will not permit a cafe until the certificate of occupancy is issued. Building code decisions can be appealed to the County's Board of Building Code Appeals within 30 days.

legal_basis.quote: Such building code shall supersede the building codes and regulations of the counties, municipalities and other political subdivisions and state agencies.
Enforcement of the provisions of the Building Code for construction and rehabilitation shall be the responsibility of the local building department.

The building official shall coordinate all reports of inspections for compliance with the Building Code, with inspections of fire and health officials delegated such authority, prior to issuance of an occupancy permit.
Any such violation shall be deemed a misdemeanor and any owner or any other person, firm, or corporation convicted of such a violation shall be punished by a fine of not more than $2,500.

It shall be unlawful for the building official or other authority to issue or allow the issuance of such permits unless the applicant has furnished his license or certificate number issued pursuant to this chapter or evidence of being exempt from the provisions of this chapter.
Application for a permit shall be made to the building official and a permit shall be obtained prior to the commencement of any of the following activities
In no case shall an applicant be required to appear in person.

An application for a permit for any proposed work shall be deemed to have been abandoned six months after the date of filing unless such application has been pursued in good faith or a permit has been issued
A permit or any amendments to an existing permit shall not be issued until the designated fees have been paid, except that the building official may authorize the delayed payment of fees.
If the application complies with the applicable requirements of this code, a permit shall be issued as soon as practicable.
Upon written request, the building official may grant one or more extensions of time, not to exceed one year per extension.
When construction reaches a stage of completion that requires an inspection, the permit holder shall notify the building official.
The building official shall either approve the work in writing or give written notice of defective work to the permit holder.

The building official shall issue the certificate of occupancy within five working days after approval of the final inspection and when the building or structure or portion thereof is determined to be in compliance with this code and any pertinent laws or ordinances, or when otherwise entitled.
The applicant shall submit a written request for appeal to the LBBCA within 30 calendar days of the receipt of the decision being appealed.

legal_basis.citation: 12VAC5-421-3660(A) (Virginia Food Regulations; why the certificate of occupancy matters to a cafe)
legal_basis.quote: Permits shall not be issued to newly constructed or extensively remodeled food establishments until a certificate of occupancy has been issued by the Building Official.

steps.step: Work out which commercial permit types the project needs
steps.who: You with your designer or general contractor; Application Services if unsure (applicationservices@albemarle.org)
steps.how: The County's commercial application types include New Commercial, Additions - Commercial Building, Commercial Alteration (the tenant up-fit used for a studio moving into existing space), Change in Building Occupancy Classification (for example turning a retail or storage space into a factory-type hot shop, or adding an assembly space for classes; the fee line is $175), Demolition, and the Electrical, Mechanical and Plumbing Sub-Permits. Alarm systems, paint spray booths and signs are separate types. A gas-fired glass furnace, glory hole and kilns are equipment under the building code (mechanical and fuel-gas work), so they need the mechanical sub-permit even if the room itself is unchanged; exhaust hoods and make-up air are mechanical; new circuits and the electrical service for kilns and annealers are electrical; a slurry sink, eyewash or cafe fixtures are plumbing.
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Commercial Building Permits page (Internet Archive copy of 16 March 2026); 13VAC5-63-80 (USBC § 108.1); Va. Code § 36-97 (definition of equipment)
steps.paraphrase: The County's page lists the commercial permit types in a table so you can pick the one to apply for.

steps.step: Clear the prerequisites: Zoning Clearance, approved site plan, VDOT approval
steps.who: You; Community Development Zoning and Planning; VDOT for a new entrance
steps.how: A new tenant's Zoning Clearance must be approved before a tenant up-fit building permit is issued (see glass_studio_zoning_use). Every commercial building permit must reference an approved Site Development Plan number and approval date, or attach the approved plan; a New Commercial application also needs VDOT approval. Alterations that change the exterior or the approved site layout may need a site plan amendment first.
steps.fee: Zoning Clearance: $60 plus 4%; site plan fees per glass_studio_zoning_use
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Commercial Building Permits page (Internet Archive copy of 16 March 2026)
steps.paraphrase: At application you must cite the approved site plan's number and date or attach the approved plan.

steps.step: Prepare the plans: building plans, a life-safety plan, mechanical and gas drawings, and any special inspections report
steps.who: Your architect or engineer; your mechanical contractor for the furnace, kilns, exhaust and gas piping
steps.how: Commercial submissions need complete building plans and, for new buildings and additions, a copy of the approved site plan; alterations need building plans and a site plan only if the exterior or site layout changes. Include a life-safety plan showing exits, travel distances, occupant loads (the class and demonstration areas set the assembly question), fire-resistance ratings and accessibility. Steel structures and other engineered systems need a Special Inspections Report with the application. For the hot shop, show the furnace, glory hole, kilns and annealers with their manufacturer data and Btu ratings, combustion air, the exhaust hoods and make-up air, clearances to combustibles, the gas piping layout and regulator, and the propane tank or natural gas meter location; these are reviewed under the mechanical and fuel-gas parts of the Uniform Statewide Building Code (the Virginia Mechanical Code and Virginia Fuel Gas Code). If you start with an approved third-party plan reviewer, every related permit must also go through third-party review.
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Application Requirements page (Internet Archive copy of 13 August 2026); 13VAC5-63 (USBC, mechanical and fuel gas provisions)
steps.paraphrase: A life-safety plan goes in with the building plans and should show exits, travel distances, occupant loads, fire ratings and accessibility.

steps.step: Line up Virginia-licensed contractors for each trade
steps.who: You; your general, mechanical (gas), electrical and plumbing contractors
steps.how: The County cannot issue a permit unless the applicant gives a Virginia DPOR contractor license number or evidence of exemption, and the applicant must show that local taxes or license fees needed to contract for the work have been paid (the County links its business license page and the DPOR license lookup from the Building Permits page). Each trade contractor applies for the sub-permit covering its own work. The owner-builder exemption in state law is for one's own primary residence, so a commercial studio build-out uses licensed contractors.
steps.basis: Va. Code § 54.1-1111(A); Albemarle County Community Development, Building Permits page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026)
steps.quote: The applicant shall also furnish satisfactory proof that the taxes or license fees required by any county, city, or town have been paid so as to be qualified to bid upon or contract for the work for which the permit has been applied.

steps.step: Register in Civic Access and submit the building permit and each trade sub-permit
steps.who: Applicant (owner, contractor or design professional); each trade contractor for its sub-permit
steps.how: Register an account in the Civic Access portal, then apply for the commercial building permit type with all documents attached (attachments are not saved in drafts). The Electrical, Mechanical and Plumbing Sub-Permits are separate applications with no required documents listed; gas piping is filed under mechanical (the fee schedule has a Gas/Oil Lines line). Fire alarm and sprinkler work are their own permits, and a sprinkler job needs the ACSA Fire Main Flushing & Testing approval. Name a mechanics' lien agent if you want one. Track the application and read reviewer comments in Civic Access; project documents are also in the County's Laserfiche document center. State rules say no applicant can be required to appear in person, and the County describes only online filing.
steps.deadline: An application not pursued in good faith is abandoned six months after filing (USBC § 108.8)
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Commercial Building Permits page (Internet Archive copy of 16 March 2026); 13VAC5-63-80 (USBC §§ 108.3, 108.8)
steps.paraphrase: You have to register in Civic Access before the County's direct application links will work.

steps.step: Plan review by Building Inspections, zoning, engineering, Fire Rescue and ACSA
steps.who: Community Development reviewers; Fire Rescue (fire prevention code plan review); the Albemarle County Service Authority where its review is required
steps.how: Reviewers post comments in Civic Access; if the plans do not comply the County must say why in writing, and you resubmit. Plan review is charged per the fee schedule (building commercial plan review $0.04 per square foot up to 5,000 square feet plus $0.03 over, minimum $15; mechanical and electrical commercial plan review $0.01 per square foot, minimum $15; plumbing $1.80 per fixture, minimum $15). Fire Rescue's Community Risk & Resilience section reviews plans for fire prevention code compliance and charges its own plan review fee ($100 per set of plans on its fee schedule). Plan amendments after submission are $35; a written code modification request is $250 with no refund.
steps.deadline: Review within a reasonable time; issuance as soon as practicable once the application complies (USBC §§ 109.4, 110.1); no local turnaround time was found
steps.fee: Building commercial plan review: $0.04 per sq. ft. for the first 5,000 sq ft, then $0.03 for each sq ft beyond that; minimum $15; mechanical and electrical commercial plan review: $0.01 per sq. ft., minimum $15; plumbing commercial plan review: $1.80 per fixture, minimum $15; permits and plan amendments $35; code modification request $250
steps.basis: Community Development fee schedule (Internet Archive copy of 20 August 2026); Fire Rescue fee schedule (effective January 19, 2022); 13VAC5-63-100 (USBC § 110.1)
steps.paraphrase: The fee schedule's line for commercial building plan review.

steps.step: Pay the invoice and receive the permits
steps.how: Fees are invoiced; pay by credit card or electronic check in the Civic Access payment portal with the invoice number, or by cash (exact change) or check in person, or by mailed check to Community Development, 401 McIntire Rd, Charlottesville, VA 22902 (no credit cards at the front desk). Permits are issued once fees are paid unless the Building Official allows delayed payment. Post the permit on site and keep a set of approved plans there. Work must start within six months and not stop for six months, or the permit can be revoked; extensions are $75 each (up to a year per extension).
steps.deadline: Fees before issuance; work started within six months of issuance (USBC § 110.6)
steps.fee: New commercial (including additions): $0.24 per sq. ft. up to 5,000 sq. ft. plus $0.17 per sq. ft. over 5,000, minimum $90; alterations, additions and repairs (all use groups): $0.20 per sq. ft., minimum $90; mechanical new commercial: $0.04 per sq. ft., minimum $90; mechanical additions, alterations and repairs: $0.04 per sq. ft., minimum $90; gas or oil lines: $40; furnace, wood stove or gas log system: $75; above-ground tanks: $120; underground tanks: $200; range hoods: $30; hood suppression systems: $35; electrical additions, alterations and repairs: $0.04 per sq. ft., minimum $90; electrical service change: $35; plumbing commercial: $10 per fixture, minimum $90; fire suppression (sprinkler): $0.95 per head, minimum $90, plus plan review $0.02 per sq. ft., minimum $75; alarm systems: $0.04 per sq. ft., minimum $90; permit extension: $75; all plus the 4% technology surcharge (see fees)
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Building Permits page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026); Community Development fee schedule; 13VAC5-63-70 (USBC § 107.1.1); 13VAC5-63-100 (USBC § 110.6)
steps.paraphrase: Card and e-check payments go through the Civic Access portal against the invoice number.

steps.step: Request inspections in Civic Access as the work reaches each stage
steps.who: Permit holder and trade contractors; County building, mechanical, electrical and plumbing inspectors; Fire Rescue for fire systems
steps.how: Request each inspection through the Civic Access portal (Dashboard, View My Permits, Inspections tab, Request Inspection; the County's next-day request deadline is 12 noon per its Inspection page). Expect rough-in and final inspections for each trade, a gas piping pressure test, and inspection of the furnace, glory hole and kiln installations, their venting and hoods, clearances and the combustion air and exhaust systems before they are concealed or fired. Provide ladders or test equipment the inspector needs. The inspector approves in writing or issues a written notice of defects; each inspection after the second of the same work is $100. Work started without a permit carries a $250 administrative fee on top of the permit fees.
steps.deadline: Notify the building official when the work reaches a stage requiring inspection, before it is covered (USBC § 113.1.2)
steps.fee: Building re-inspection (each inspection after the second of the same work): $100; administrative fee for working without a permit: $250
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Commercial Building Permits page (Internet Archive copy of 16 March 2026); Community Development fee schedule; 13VAC5-63-130 (USBC §§ 113.1.2, 113.6)
steps.paraphrase: Inspections are requested in the Civic Access portal with a registered account.

steps.step: Pass the final inspections and get the certificate of occupancy (or a temporary one)
steps.who: Permit holder; Building Official; Fire Rescue and the Health Department where they have delegated inspections; zoning final inspection
steps.how: After the final building and trade inspections, the final zoning inspection ($25) and any fire and health sign-offs, the Building Official issues the certificate of occupancy within five working days of approving the final inspection. Do not occupy or open before it issues. If part of the building is safe to use while other work continues, a Commercial Temporary Certificate of Occupancy is $150 for each 30 days. The Health Department will not issue a food establishment permit for a newly built or extensively remodeled cafe until the certificate of occupancy exists, and ACSA needs at least a signed building permit before it schedules a water meter.
steps.deadline: Certificate of occupancy within five working days after approval of the final inspection (USBC § 116.1)
steps.fee: Commercial Temporary Certificate of Occupancy: $150 for each 30 days; zoning final inspection: $25
steps.basis: 13VAC5-63-160 (USBC § 116.1); Va. Code § 36-105(B); Community Development fee schedule; 12VAC5-421-3660(A)
steps.paraphrase: The fee schedule's line for a commercial temporary certificate of occupancy, charged for each 30 days.

steps.step: Keep the equipment in code after opening, and permit later changes
steps.how: Replacing or adding a furnace, kiln or gas appliance, extending gas piping, adding electrical circuits or changing the exhaust later each needs a new trade permit (gas or oil fueled appliance replacement is not exempt). Changing the use of a room (for example turning storage into a classroom or a cafe) is a Change in Building Occupancy Classification. Keep the manufacturer data and permit records; the Fire Marshal's annual inspections (glass_studio_fire_permits) look for them.
steps.fee: Mechanical furnace or gas appliance: $75; gas or oil lines: $40; change of occupancy classification: $175; plus 4%
steps.paraphrase: The fee schedule's mechanical line for gas or oil piping.

escalation.trigger: Permit denied, plans rejected, a failed inspection or notice of defective work, a refused code modification, a stop work order, or a refused certificate of occupancy
escalation.next: Albemarle County Board of Building Code Appeals (written appeal filed with the code official; fee $350 plus 4%)
escalation.deadline: Written request within 30 calendar days of receipt of the decision; the board meets within 30 calendar days of the application (up to 45 with regular monthly meetings)
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 36-105(A); 13VAC5-63-190 (USBC §§ 119.5, 119.6); Community Development fee schedule
escalation.quote: The applicant shall submit a written request for appeal to the LBBCA within 30 calendar days of the receipt of the decision being appealed.

escalation.trigger: Disagree with the local board's decision
escalation.next: State Building Code Technical Review Board (DHCD), on its Application for Administrative Appeal
escalation.deadline: 21 calendar days after receipt of the local board's decision
escalation.quote: The application for appeal shall be made to the State Review Board within 21 calendar days of the receipt of the decision to be appealed.

escalation.trigger: The County cannot make a requested inspection within two working days
escalation.next: Reports from an approved third-party inspector under the building official's written policy, which the building official reviews and must accept or reject in writing within two working days
escalation.quote: Under circumstances where the building official is unable to make the inspection or test required by Section 113.3 or 113.4 within two working days of a request or an agreed upon date or if authorized for other circumstances in the building official's written policy, the building official shall accept reports for review.

caveats: www.albemarle.org refuses automated readers; the County pages cited are Internet Archive copies (dates in the sources) and the County's quotes carry paraphrases because its terms bar reposting.

The County's commercial permit pages do not describe how a glass furnace, glory hole or kiln is classified or inspected; the mechanical and fuel-gas treatment in s3 and s8 follows the Uniform Statewide Building Code's structure (the Virginia Mechanical Code and Fuel Gas Code are parts of 13VAC5-63) and should be confirmed with Building Inspections at the pre-application meeting. Whether the hot shop is reviewed as a Factory (F-1) occupancy, and whether a classroom or demonstration area is an Assembly occupancy, are Building Official decisions.

Fees come from the Community Development fee schedule capture of 20 August 2026 and apply through December 31, 2026; the schedule adopted April 22, 2026 takes effect January 1, 2027 and its amounts were not read. The State's 2% Building Code Academy levy and how it appears on invoices was not confirmed (see building_permit_residential).
The Civic Access portal was not opened; no account was created and nothing was submitted. Portal steps follow the County's how-to PDFs cited in building_permit_residential.
Documents named but not read: the Special Inspections Report Packet, the Building Permit Information Guide, and the ACSA Fire Main Flushing & Testing form.
The Fire Rescue plan review fee ($100 per set of plans) is read from a scanned fee table whose columns are hard to align; confirm with the Fire Marshal's Office.
